<!-- pr-reviewer: aba806180dd84b4b546bd01f951c64c8c29e5bd0 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers; two non-blocking notes below.

### What looks good
- Provenance is named in every new module (APPNOTE.TXT for the ZIP reader, FIPS 180-4 for SHA-256, tangency-labs/solidcraft Apache-2.0 files and functions for the container/cache layout, solidcore-record `native::decode` for the body) and the mod.rs header says no layout was derived from sample bytes. Nothing reads as byte guessing.
- Untrusted-input handling is thorough: 256 MiB file cap, 10,000-entry cap checked before the directory loop, per-entry caps checked on the declared size before inflating and again by `take(size + 1)` (so a lying header cannot bomb), length and CRC-32 checked, directory/local-header/data ranges all through `checked_add` and `get`, ZIP64/multi-disk/encrypted refused, entry names only compared (never a path), serde_json's recursion limit bounds nesting, manifest lists capped, slice offsets contiguous and `checked_add`ed. No unwrap/expect/panic in the new code; a decoder or kernel panic is caught and reported, and the kernel is reset after it.
- Correctness is pinned: the sample's exact box equals the design parameters (125 mm diameter, 85 mm height) to 1e-6. mm only; inch and any other unit refused by name. A stale cache (document digest) and a payload digest mismatch are refused; several bodies, placed copies and mesh bodies are refused by name.
- `build_record` split is behaviour-neutral for STEP (suites below green). Fixture is 2.5 MB (the PR text says 5 MB), marked binary, read as data only. Decision file lists the dependency, why a crate was not added, and what rebuilds; `Refs #1456`, `Changelog: none`, follow-up #1463 named; files all under 400 lines; no process files, snapshots or CHANGELOG touched.

### Results (merged with main, local build, no Actions run)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --test solidcraft_import` | 7 passed (40.8 s) |
| kernel lib `solidcraft` (SHA-256 vectors) | 1 passed |
| `step_import` / `corrupt_input` / `machining_mesh` | 3 / 6 / 5 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Mutation checks: with the stale-document check disabled, `a_cache_that_is_not_this_documents_is_refused` failed ("stale: imported 'Body1' instead of refusing"); with the units check disabled, `documents_we_cannot_read_are_refused` failed ("inch: imported ..."). Both reverted. Other refusal tests were not mutation-checked.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. `damaged_files_never_panic_or_hang`: 48 of the 64 copies damage the raw `.sc`, where almost every hit lands in deflate data and stops at the CRC-32 check, so the body decoder and `build_record` are barely exercised by it. The manifest cases do reach the table logic. A mutation of the body bytes behind a re-keyed digest (like the "garbled" case, but seeded and repeated) would cover the decoder and kernel path where a hang could actually live. The hang guard itself is real (cancel token, then a panic if no answer), but it only helps where the kernel polls the token. A follow-up is fine.
2. NaN/huge coordinates are not refused in this module; they rely on `build_record`'s existing checks (healing, integrity, measure, vertex gap), shared with STEP. I did not exercise a NaN-coordinate body. Worth one test with the app wiring.
3. Not exercised: release mode, other OSes, no app/MCP path exists yet (stated in the PR). The machining mesh refusal for this body is #1463.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
